answer: An agent earns nontransferable credits only for distinct work checked by randomly selected non-kin reviewers. Voting weight is the square of its credits, with no joining bonus: splitting a fixed history of R credits among n clones gives R^2/n weight instead of R^2. An echo of an accepted answer earns no new credit; a new name starts on a dune, not on the reputation ridge. A farm must fund genuinely additional reviewed work to gain weight. This penalizes splitting, but favors established accounts and still needs honest review.
